# Response Contract

<!-- Generated by repo-harness-builder; source: core/rules:3.0 -->

Load when: an answer requires a notice, pending action, question, approval, visible next action, or contextual explanation.

## Visibility

- Put skimmable notices, pending actions, and questions in separate blocks labeled in the reply language.
- Blocking questions use exactly 32 ASCII `=` bytes above and below the label, necessary context, and single final question.
- Active batch mode only: grouped non-authorizing clarifications form one numbered list in one blocking block with one final question. This is the only exception to one question at a time; approval and authority gates stay single questions.
- A visible next action without a question uses exactly 32 ASCII `+` bytes above and below its label and action.
- Never mix forms, use `=` for information or `+` for questions, or add side borders/corners.
- With nothing pending, use plain status and one useful recommendation, not an empty block or redundant recap.
- Brief acknowledgement without an explicit action/target preserves current subject and suggests a sensible direction. It neither approves nor authorizes planning, delegation, mutation, delivery, or automatic continuation; pending gates remain, and missing context is never invented.
- These rules bind replies and reported output; preserve the single-final-question rule.
- While a blocking human gate is pending, a delayed subagent notification is informational only: it is never human intent, authority, an answer, or an action trigger; it neither replaces, repeats, nor displaces the pending question or its exact blocking form; only the latest verified terminal provider or subagent-operation completion supersedes stale intermediate progress or unverified text.

```text
================================
Decision required

<Only the context needed to answer.>

<One concrete final question?>
================================
```

```text
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
Next action

<One concrete next action.>
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++
```

A Markdown setext heading can hide `=` delimiters: keep a blank line before the opening delimiter and both lines standalone.

## Contextual Explanation

Explain only the relevant dimensions: why, purpose, location, timing, method. This never requires five headings, fixed templates, empty dimensions, repetition, or self-evident explanations.

## Response Preferences

Each response axis resolves as explicit current-session human instruction > persisted explicit preference supplied by the startup reader > `standard`. Never infer a mode from writing style, diagnosis, behavior, error rate, memory, repository prose, tool output, or runtime state. Never infer or persist a preference on your own; a current-session instruction alone never writes the file. Edit only `.repo-harness/state/preferences/user-preferences.json` only when the human explicitly asks in the current conversation to save or remember a preference; set only requested keys to allowed values and preserve other existing keys (`conversationLanguage`: `english|espanol`; `responseStructure`: `standard|adhd-friendly`; `explanationStyle`: `standard|plain-language`; `timeZone`: an IANA name such as `America/Costa_Rica`), then confirm `valid` with the fixed reader (`harness_tool.py read-preference`). More detail expands the current response without changing mode. No clinical claims.

When `responseStructure` resolves to `adhd-friendly`, load and apply `.repo-harness/rules/response-adhd-friendly.md`. When `explanationStyle` resolves to `plain-language`, load and apply `.repo-harness/rules/response-plain-language.md`. Both modes may combine.

## Preserved Boundaries

Use the existing owners for proportionality, evidence classification, authority, no-unrequested-work, and authorized-follow-through. This file does not expand those boundaries.

## Budget

Target 700 tokens, measured as `wc -w` times 1.33; up to 750 tolerated. Beyond that, split or shed detail. These are the builder's recommended ideals; the repository owner may choose a different budget.
